slot.brief: Given two groups with known means and variances, find the combined mean and combined variance using pooled formulas.

stem: Two groups of sizes $40$ and $60$ have means $25$ and $35$, and variances $14$ and $9$, respectively. The variance of the combined group of $100$ observations is
working:
Let the two groups have sizes $n_1 = 40$ and $n_2 = 60$, means $\bar{x}_1 = 25$ and $\bar{x}_2 = 35$, and variances $\sigma_1^2 = 14$ and $\sigma_2^2 = 9$.

1. Calculate the combined mean $\bar{x}$:
$$\bar{x} = \dfrac{n_1 \bar{x}_1 + n_2 \bar{x}_2}{n_1 + n_2} = \dfrac{40(25) + 60(35)}{40 + 60} = \dfrac{1000 + 2100}{100} = 31$$

2. Compute the deviations from the combined mean:
$$d_1 = \bar{x}_1 - \bar{x} = 25 - 31 = -6 \implies d_1^2 = 36$$
$$d_2 = \bar{x}_2 - \bar{x} = 35 - 31 = 4 \implies d_2^2 = 16$$

3. Calculate the combined variance $\sigma^2$:
$$\sigma^2 = \dfrac{n_1(\sigma_1^2 + d_1^2) + n_2(\sigma_2^2 + d_2^2)}{n_1 + n_2}$$
$$\sigma^2 = \dfrac{40(14 + 36) + 60(9 + 16)}{100} = \dfrac{40(50) + 60(25)}{100} = \dfrac{2000 + 1500}{100} = 35$$

Independent check: Combined mean = (40·25+60·35)/100 = 31. Deviations d1=−6, d2=4. Combined variance = [40(14+36)+60(9+16)]/100 = (2000+1500)/100 = 35.
